hints: A rearrangement of code has exactly the same length and letter counts as code. So which pieces of the message are worth checking?
Use a fixed-size sliding window of length |code| over message, keeping 26 letter counts and comparing them to the counts of code.

1. If code is longer than message, return false.
  2. Count letters of code into need.
  3. Slide over message: add the entering letter, remove the one that falls out once the window exceeds |code|.
  4. If the counts match at any full window, return true.
  5. Return false.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: For every piece of length |code|, sort it and compare with sorted code.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Fixed-size window with 26 counts, updated by one letter in and one out per step.

explain: For code "tac" and message "xxactz": the windows are xxa, xac, act. The third has one each of a, c, t, the same as the code, so we return true. Comparing two 26-length arrays is constant work, so the whole scan is linear. Always check the length first, because a code longer than the message can never fit.
recognize: Does any substring permute into a given word? → fixed-size window with letter counts.
